The pilot had declared that the engine had stalled and that he was trying to reach Reindeer Island. He then stated that he was going into the water. Two RCMP and an Air Search and Rescue Hercules aircrafts conducted an aerial search. It was not possible to search the lake by boat as there was too much ice on the lake. All three are presumed dead from drowning or the impact of the crash.

Case reference: 2014002167.CaseDesc: On July 7, 1973, William Gorrie and his family were seen by a an RCMP patrol boat returning from a day of fishing in Cross Bay, Manitoba. The waves increased in height and he followed the patrol boat, eventually getting his family on board. As a result, the patrol boat had to increase its power, significantly increasing the distance between the two boats. The last sighting of Mr. Gorrie's boat was approximately 1 km behind the patrol boat. An immediate search by air was conducted with negative results. It is presumed that William drowned as neither he nor the boat were ever located.

Case reference: 2013000092.CaseDesc: Jacques Boulanger was last seen on September 1, 1989 in Montreal, Quebec. Jacques loved sleeping outside even though he had a home and was a cabinetmaker in his spare time.  He might have a scar on his leg or foot.

Case reference: 2014003840.CaseDesc: On December 7, 1986, a male was seen floating in the river. The male initially responded to police calls however shortly after he was observed going under the water. It is presumed he drowned. The identity of the male was unknown to police until Roderick Cook's parents contacted police advising they had not seen their son for some time. It is assumed the man in the river was Roderick based both on the description and the fact that he was seen walking near the river. Police further found footprints that led from the shore to the open water. No foul play is suspected in this matter and it is assumed Roderick drowned.

Teeth: Two front upper teeth are false

Case reference: 2013000068.CaseDesc: On October 27, 1994, Yvon Ringuet was reported missing from his home in the Rosemont-La Petite-Patrie district in Montreal, Quebec. Yvon would call or visit his mother everyday. All his personal belongings were found in his home and no one has seen or heard from him since.

Tattoo: Cross, right or left upper arm
